entries.title: Adding Temperature to the Adiabatic Connection: Hybrid Functionals for Static and Dynamic Correlation
entries.summary: Capturing static and dynamic electron correlation simultaneously at manageable computational cost remains a key challenge in electronic structure theory. Motivated by the recurring role of effective temperature in self-consistent field methods we extend the adiabatic connection mechanism from density functional theory to include a temperature dimension. This gives rise to thermally enhanced hybrid functionals, in which static correlation is captured via fractional occupations generated by an effective "correlation temperature" within thermal Hartree-Fock, while dynamic correlation is described by established density functional approximations. The framework formally unifies information-density matrix functional theory (i-DMFT) and thermally-assisted-occupation (TAO-)DFT as special cases, clarifying their theoretical basis and the respective prescriptions for the temperature parameter. We assess the performance of several thermally enhanced hybrids for different cases where i-DMFT was previously shown to fail. Furthermore, we discuss and test different schemes for determining the correlation temperature and investigate the accuracy of different such choices for a benchmark set derived from biphenyl. The results help to clarify the achievable balance of accuracy, generality, and efficiency, establishing thermally enhanced hybrids as a systematic route toward low-cost treatment of both correlation types.

entries.title: Thermal activation of photon catalysis in difference-intensity Mach-Zehnder interferometry with squeezed thermal light
entries.summary: Realistic non-Gaussian operations, which can be implemented by mixing a nonclassical Gaussian state with a Fock state at a beam splitter and then heralding on a photon-number-resolving detector, are known to improve phase estimation in a Mach-Zehnder interferometer. The existing studies have considered the single-mode squeezed vacuum for difference-intensity and parity detection, and the two-mode squeezed thermal state for parity detection alone as the initial Gaussian resources. However, a real squeezer in the lab actually produces single-mode squeezed thermal light, which has not been studied in a coherent-plus-resource interferometer. We take up this case and using the phase space Wigner picture, we obtain the heralded state produced by photon subtraction, addition and catalysis on a single-mode squeezed thermal resource, and evaluate the corresponding phase sensitivities. Single-photon catalysis, which is useless on squeezed vacuum, becomes a useful operation for any thermal occupation above $\nth\simeq0.2$, and since it heralds with a probability near one-half, it turns out to be the best success-weighted operation over the whole thermal range. In the vacuum limit our results reproduce the known hierarchy, where two-photon catalysis is the best operation. The quantum Fisher information computations confirms that thermal noise enhances the phase information encoded in the catalyzed state, demonstrating that difference-intensity detection closely approaches the ultimate precision bound across most operational regimes, and, together with a loss analysis, verifies the robustness of the effect.

entries.title: Sluggish random walks with resetting: nonequilibrium aspects
entries.summary: We derive exact analytical expressions for the fixed-time probability distribution and the Laplace transform of the distribution of the first-passage time to reach a target for a sluggish random walk in one dimension subject to two different types of stochastic resetting: stochastic resetting at random Poisson-distributed times, and resetting implemented whenever a position threshold is reached. The optimal resetting rate that minimises the mean first-passage time is obtained as a function of the sluggishness parameter, while under threshold resetting the mean first-passage time to the origin is found to increase monotonically with the threshold. We also characterise the occupation-time statistics, retrieving a Lamperti-type distribution under free dynamics and under Poissonian resetting at rate for short observation times, a Gaussian distribution centred at half for long observation times, and a distinct deterministic limit under threshold resetting. To further characterise nonequilibrium aspects of resetting, we evaluate the distribution and mean of the cost incurred per reset under Poissonian resetting, and the cost rate under threshold resetting, for different (linear, power-law, exponential) cost functions, and find the same critical behaviour of the cost rate in the limits of a vanishing resetting rate and an infinite threshold, respectively. Numerical simulations validate with excellent accuracy our analytical formulae.

entries.title: Localisation of the monkey walk with an "impurity" at the origin
entries.summary: The monkey walk is a model of reinforced random walk introduced by Boyer and Solis-Salas as a model for the exploratory behaviour of capuchin monkeys. At each step of the walk, the walker flips a biased coin to determine whether to take a simple, symmetric random walk step on $\mathbb{Z}^d$ or to "relocate", i.e. choose a time uniformly at random in its past and jump to where it was at that time. More recently, Boyer, Falcón-Cortés, Giuggioli and Majumdar looked at a modification of the model, where the probability to relocate is $ξ_0$ when the walker sits at the origin and $ξ>ξ_0$ anywhere else. We prove that, for all $ξ_0\in (0,1)$, if $ξ$ is sufficiently close to 1, then the monkey walk "localises", i.e. the position of the walker at time $n$, $W_n$, converges in distribution without any renormalisation. (We in fact prove convergence of the occupation measure of the walker.) This is in contrast with the case when $ξ= ξ_0$, for which it is known that $W_n/\sqrt{\log n}$ converges in distribution to a standard Gaussian (we say that the walk "diffuses"). Our proof relies on seeing the monkey walk as an infinitely-many colour Pólya urn (a.k.a. measure-valued Pólya process - MVPP) and then prove convergence of this urn, which is not straightforward as theorems from the literature on MVPPs do not apply directly.

entries.title: Synthetic populations for epidemic, demographic and mobility modeling
entries.summary: Synthetic populations are essential for individual-based simulations, such as agent-based models, enabling the evaluation of policy interventions for epidemic control, demographic studies and mobility management, to mention a few. Existing synthetic populations are often designed for specific settings and rarely combine nationwide coverage with realistic and explicit spatial detail. This limits their ability to represent realistic spatial relationships and interplay between households, workplaces, leisure activities, and mobility patterns, reducing models utility for targeted decision-making. Here, we present a harmonized dataset of synthetic populations taking as case studies Spain, France, and Italy. Despite heterogeneous census data sources and formats, we release a unified data structure ensuring consistency and interoperability. The synthetic population generation pipeline reproduces household composition, population density, age-sex structure, and occupation distribution at census-tract level, enriched with municipality-level commuting flows and economic activity patterns. Country-specific pre-processing, statistical calibration, and data integration produce coherent demographic and spatial characteristics suitable for large-scale, country-agnostic simulations. As the pipeline relies on publicly available census data, it is readily extensible to other countries, supporting high-resolution modeling of infectious diseases, hazard exposure, demographic analysis, and urban mobility.

entries.title: Policy-Gradient Transfer under a Shared State Estimator
entries.summary: This paper considers the problem of policy-gradient transfer from a simulator to a physical plant when both are controlled through the same fixed state estimator. The plant and the simulator are partially observed nonlinear systems with additive Gaussian noise of common known covariance whose dynamics and observation models differ, and the controller is a squashed Gaussian policy with uniformly bounded latent mean and first two parameter derivatives. We derive a bound on the difference between the plant and simulator policy gradients that is linear in the noise-weighted model error and requires no estimator-accuracy guarantee, because the shared estimator is a common post-processing of the measurements and the data-processing inequality compares the trajectory laws without an estimation-error term. Based on this bound, we derive an occupancy-weighted refinement, a sufficient condition for the simulator gradient to be an ascent direction for the plant, and a bound on the expected squared plant gradient at a random iterate of a finite simulator-training run with optimization, truncation and model-error terms. Simulation results on a scalar system and a pendulum are presented to validate the theoretical results.

entries.title: Decision-FLIP: Budget-Free Structured Pruning for Gaussian Occupancy Models
entries.summary: Occupancy predictors rely on large persistent banks of Gaussians or learned queries whose size is fixed by hand. Common pruning proxies, such as opacity, activation frequency, or parameter magnitude, do not measure whether removing a row changes the model's voxel decisions. We introduce Decision-FLIP, a budget-free compilation framework whose scoring and structure selection need only unlabeled calibration inputs. Exact Mean-FLIP scores each persistent row by the number of voxel argmax decisions that change when the row is removed from the readout; a guarded Otsu split of the log-score distribution selects the survivor count without a target and abstains when the split is unsupported; and the survivors are physically compiled into a smaller checkpoint, so camera sampling, attention, and aggregation shrink with the bank. For streaming banks, scores are integrated over each row's lifecycle through warp, death, and refill. Across four Gaussian-bank model-dataset settings and one persistent-query transfer, the automatically selected cuts remove 12-79% of eligible rows and cut bank/query-dependent latency by 7-45% across settings with component profiles, with whole-model savings of up to 8.0% on the primary endpoints bounded by fixed-cost image, voxel, and sensor modules and peak-memory savings of up to 16.6%. Under matched one-epoch recovery controls, semantic mIoU changes by at most 0.18 point. Same-$K$ controls show that the ranking, not only the bank size, matters: random removal collapses GaussianFormer-1 and OccFormer, while label-free Mean-FLIP matches or outperforms supervised Taylor ranking on all five settings where that control was run. The method applies when removable primitives keep a stable checkpoint-row identity; it is budget-free in survivor count, not parameter-free.

entries.title: GS-PRM: Gaussian Visual Roadmap for Image-Goal Navigation
entries.summary: Image-goal navigation requires a global planner that connects visually specified endpoints while providing observations that a local policy can follow. Three-dimensional Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) provides map-registered RGB, opacity, and depth renderings, but does not explicitly encode navigable topology. We introduce GS-PRM, a Gaussian visual roadmap whose milestones, local connections, and visual references are constructed directly through 3DGS rendering without deriving an occupancy grid or signed distance field. We define render-based collision-free (RC-free) configurations and paths. Panoramic depth supplies conservative clearance for milestone validation and adaptive coverage, while edge-aligned orthographic rendering tests the robot's swept volume. We establish conditional soundness and sufficient conditions for deterministic query completeness and probabilistic construction completeness of GS-PRM. To validate the performance of GS-PRM, we conduct experiments in both simulated and real-world environments, demonstrating long-horizon navigation using goal-conditioned policies guided by GS-PRM. Compared with a state-of-the-art 3DGS-based navigation system, our GS-PRM-based navigation system achieves up to a twice higher average success rate and reduces travel time by up to 57.2% when both systems complete the navigation task.

entries.title: Multi-Agent Path Planning via Compatible Encounter-Space Allocation in Crowded Spaces Dynamically Occupied by Work Activities
entries.summary: Lifelong multiagent path planning on construction floors must accommodate continually changing goals and work occupancy. Existing planners can update paths and timing online, but work motion space coupling changes the spatial basis of unfinished encounters, while rerouting affects later encounters. Planning must therefore construct and maintain local encounter possibility. We propose Width based Planning with Compatible Encounter Space Allocation (WP), which constructs shared passage relationships from actual encounter demands and real time widths. Shared channels, ordered anchors, and urgency based updates coordinate successive encounters while retaining individual greedy motion between them. A necessary and sufficient width condition for fixed-point position exchange and a necessary directional condition for composite exchange provide geometric grounds for channel construction and encounter relocation. In crowded floor computational experiments, WP maintained route continuation after occupancy changes and enabled multi agent clearing, with infrequent, brief near stops. Complete run comparisons with four methods showed 25.2% to 52.2% more mean goal arrivals than the best baseline at each configuration of 5 to 10 agents, with lower mean computation time than the rolling horizon K_CBS adaptation. The contribution is a planning principle that constructs and continuously maintains local passage relationships from real time space, unifying shared spatial allocation and conditional local clearing to extend lifelong planning to work motion space coupling.

entries.title: Limit Theorems for the Complete Feedback Card Guessing Game
entries.summary: We study the optimal score $T_{n,m}$ in a complete feedback card guessing game. The deck has $n$ types and $m$ cards of each type. Its predictable compensator $S_{n,m}$ is the sum of the conditional success probabilities. We prove that Var$(S_{n,m})\leq C((\log\log n)^2+m/\log n)$, uniformly in $m$ for large $n$. This bound yields a central limit theorem for every sequence $m=m_n\geq1$ as $n\to\infty$. The score variance is asymptotic to its mean. We also give uniform Kolmogorov bounds using the conditional Bernoulli moments. For $m,n\to\infty$, the excess mean is asymptotic to $(\log n)\log\min\{m,\log n\}+(π/\sqrt2)\sqrt{m\log n}$. The two contributions balance at $m\asymp(\log n)(\log\log n)^2$. The variance proof uses reversed occupancy hitting times. Discrete hypergeometric tail estimates control their fluctuations in the large-deviation, Gaussian, and saturation regimes. For fixed $n$, we also show that the compensator has a Brownian-bridge functional limit as $m\to\infty$.

entries.title: GNFormer: Gaussian Neural Field Transformer for Efficient Camera-based Occupancy Prediction
entries.summary: Camera-based occupancy prediction provides geometric and semantic scene understanding for robot perception and has been adopted in autonomous vehicle and UAV perception systems. Gaussian primitives offer a promising alternative by potentially representing only occupied regions, thereby concentrating computation and representational capacity where needed and reducing wasted computation and memory in empty space. However, existing Gaussian-based methods suffer from poor primitive utilization, as ineffective training objectives leave some Gaussians in empty space, while the limited expressiveness of Gaussian functions restricts their ability to model complex shapes. To address these limitations, we propose a novel 3D representation, Gaussian Neural Field (GNF), which can accurately map voxel positions to semantic occupancies. In GNF, Gaussians and a neural network jointly parameterize the field, where the Gaussians define its spatial support and provide features for neural decoding, while the neural network enables more expressive occupancy modeling than Gaussian functions alone. We further develop the Gaussian Neural Field Transformer (GNFormer), a streamlined and flexible method that predicts GNFs for camera-based occupancy prediction. Across Occ-ScanNet, SSCBench-KITTI-360, and nuScenes-SurroundOcc benchmarks, GNFormer achieves the highest IoU and mIoU and the fastest inference among the compared single-frame methods. In the experiments, GNFormer can represent indoor and outdoor scenes with only 256 and 1024 Gaussians, respectively, substantially fewer primitives than prior Gaussian-based methods. The code will be released.

entries.title: Finite-temperature adiabatic-connection reduced density-matrix functional theory: a unified framework for i-DMFT and TAO-DFT
entries.summary: Accurately describing chemical bond breaking requires capturing strong/static electron correlation, a major challenge for single-reference self-consistent-field methods such as Hartree--Fock and Kohn--Sham density-functional theory (DFT). Fractional occupations substantially improve this situation, as demonstrated by information-density-matrix-functional theory (i-DMFT) and thermally-assisted-occupation DFT (TAO-DFT). Although useful, they are formulated within rather different theoretical frameworks, are somewhat semi-empirical, and their relationship remains unclear. Here we introduce finite-temperature adiabatic-connection reduced density-matrix functional theory (FT-AC-RDMFT), in which i-DMFT and TAO-DFT emerge as different reductions of a unified framework. The effective eigenvalue equation for natural orbitals and the Fermi--Dirac occupation numbers follow directly from the variational principle, while a thermal adiabatic connection relates the empirical entropy coefficient of i-DMFT to a characteristic temperature of the auxiliary non-interacting system. Within this framework, i-DMFT is the exact-exchange-based reduction, whereas TAO-DFT results when exact exchange is replaced by a density-based exchange-correlation functional. Numerical calculations confirm that i-DMFT, apart from a constant, coincides with the exact-exchange realization of the framework, and show that the improved dissociation behavior from finite-temperature occupations extends beyond exact exchange to hybrid and semilocal density functionals. For strongly correlated V2O3, finite-temperature occupations substantially reduce the severely overestimated non-magnetic LDA bulk modulus, bringing it close to experiment. These results establish FT-AC-RDMFT as a common theoretical foundation for finite-temperature occupation-based electronic-structure methods in molecular and solid-state systems.

entries.title: Fine-Tuning Strategy, Not Just Data: A Statistically Rigorous Audit of Gender and Stereotypical Bias in Embedding Models for HR Recommendation Systems
entries.summary: Embedding models underpin modern job-candidate matching: resumes, job descriptions, and queries are encoded as dense vectors, and recommendations come from nearest-neighbor retrieval over that space. Any social bias in the embeddings therefore feeds directly into HR recommendations. We audit six multilingual sentence-embedding models (LaBSE- and E5-family, both public and custom fine-tuned) using Bias-in-Bios (occupational gender bias) and StereoSet (stereotypes across profession, race, gender, and religion). We treat statistical validity as a first-class concern: we identify a non-independence error in a naive significance test, where pooling non-independent pairwise similarities inflated a trivial 0.0046 mean difference to $p \approx 0$, and replace it with a profession-level paired Wilcoxon signed-rank test, individual-resampling bootstrap confidence intervals, and permutation tests for StereoSet. Under the corrected methodology, knowledge-distillation (KD) fine-tuning of E5-Base significantly increases measured bias on Bias-in-Bios ($Δ= -0.177$, $p < 10^{-8}$; more negative means more bias), although this measure is sensitive to global embedding geometry. The KD result is corroborated by pro-stereotype patterns in the StereoSet profession category (uncorrected $p < 0.05$). Binary-classification fine-tuning of the same base model shows no statistically distinguishable change ($p = 0.218$). Fine-tuning strategy is thus an actionable design lever for practitioners building HR recommenders. We also report which benchmark categories are underpowered, and note that two domain-adapted models could not be included in significance testing due to a software-access constraint, which limits our conclusions.

entries.title: From Field to Planning: Learning Temporal Polar Gradient Fields for Vision-based AAV Trajectory Planning in Dynamic Environments
entries.summary: Autonomous Aerial Vehicle (AAV) trajectory planning requires real-time and accurate safety gradient guidance, especially in dynamic environments. Existing methods typically rely on static maps and dynamic obstacle tracking to construct gradient fields, imposing heavy computational burdens and yielding conservative trajectories. To address these limitations, we propose a two-stage Field-to-Planning (F2P) learning framework to provide accurate and efficient safety gradients for trajectory planning in dynamic environments. In the first stage, we introduce an Ego-centric Polar Occupancy (EPO) representation that naturally matches the geometry of the onboard camera frustum, while supporting unstructured scene modeling. Subsequently, we formulate a Temporal Polar Gradient Field (TPGF) via multi-kernel separable Gaussian convolution to provide unified safety gradients, without explicitly distinguishing between static and dynamic obstacles. To mitigate the inherent spatial ambiguity introduced by applying convolutions within the polar grid, we propose an ESDF-guided offline learning strategy that incorporates geometric priors into TPGF. In the second stage, we employ the calibrated TPGF to guide the trajectory planning policy in a self-supervised learning manner. Comparative results with other approaches demonstrate the superiority of our method. Extensive real-world experiments within various cluttered dynamic environments validate the real-time performance and robustness on resource-constrained onboard systems.

entries.title: Quantum dynamics of an ion in an RF quadrupole trap with weak octupolar anharmonicity
entries.summary: We investigate the quantum dynamics of a single ion confined in a radio-frequency (RF) Paul trap in the presence of weak octupole-induced anharmonicity, as can occur in realistic ion-trap potential. The explicitly time-dependent quadrupole potential is treated in a reference-oscillator Fock basis, allowing the effects of the RF drive and the quartic correction to be resolved directly at the level of motional-state couplings. While the quadratic RF interaction generates $Δn=\pm2$ transitions and Gaussian squeezing, the quartic contribution opens additional $Δn=\pm4$ coupling pathways. Starting from the reference-oscillator vacuum, we show that the octupole interaction broadens the even-parity Fock-state distribution and enhances the phonon-number fluctuations more strongly than the mean occupation. At the same time, the RF-induced sub-vacuum quadrature squeezing remains robust, although its magnitude and orientation are modified by the quartic interaction. The number statistics and quadrature fluctuations therefore respond differently to the same nonlinear perturbation, reflecting the distinct roles of Fock-space redistribution and phase coherence. The resulting dynamics provide a quantum-mechanical characterization of weak octupole corrections beyond the ideal quadrupole approximation and clarify how realistic anharmonicities modify nonclassical trapped-ion motion. Importantly, the motional nonclassicality remains robust against the weak octupole perturbation, as evidenced by persistent sub-vacuum quadrature squeezing and Klyshko-inequality violation. These results characterize how realistic anharmonic corrections reshape trapped-ion motion beyond the ideal quadrupole approximation.

entries.title: Control-Ready Uncertainty for Trajectory Diffusion
entries.summary: Diffusion models can represent complex, multimodal trajectory distributions, but extracting uncertainty from them typically requires costly Monte Carlo sampling. This limits their use in real-time control, where robots must rapidly assess risk and maintain safety margins. We introduce Score-Curvature for Online Precision Estimation (SCOPE), a lightweight module that augments diffusion trajectory models with control-ready uncertainty. SCOPE learns a structured precision matrix around each nominal trajectory by distilling score-curvature information and producing calibrated Gaussian tubes with low overhead and without repeated Monte Carlo sampling. These tubes provide per-timestep covariance estimates that can be used both as predicted occupancy for moving agents and as adaptive exploration guides for robot control. We evaluate SCOPE with mode-conditioned multimodal diffusion backbones in pedestrian forecasting, crowd navigation, Maze2D control, and real-world Franka Panda manipulation. Across these settings, SCOPE provides fast uncertainty estimation, which leads to better closed-loop performance. Project page: https://zackaxue.github.io/SCOPE-project-page/

entries.title: A Unified Bellman Operator for Safety-Critical Reinforcement Learning
entries.summary: Reinforcement learning in safety-critical domains requires maximizing task performance while strictly adhering to safety constraints. Existing safe reinforcement learning paradigms typically force a trade-off: they either require a priori knowledge to provide strict safety guarantees (e.g., safety filters), or they enable joint learning but only satisfy safety constraints on average. In this work, we propose a novel Bellman operator that unifies performance and safety objectives into a joint value function. We show that temporal difference learning with the joint Bellman operator converges under a two-timescale stochastic approximation framework. On the fast timescale, the safety value of the learning joint policy is estimated, while the joint value is estimated on the slow timescale. Convergence is ensured by formulating the limiting dynamics as an occupation-averaged differential inclusion, and showing that it asymptotically converges to a set of limiting optimal safety-constrained task value functions. Theoretically, once converged, the resulting optimal policy maximizes task return while maintaining safety at all times. Empirical evaluations on continuous control tasks with neural approximations demonstrate stable convergence with near-zero safety violations at test time.

entries.title: Construction-Dependent Floquet Topology in Circularly Driven $N$-Stacked Su-Schrieffer-Heeger Chains
entries.summary: We investigate construction-dependent Floquet topology in a two-dimensional lattice formed by stacking Su-Schrieffer-Heeger (SSH) chains with co-located sublattice orbitals. We present two constructions in the decoupled-chain limit. Construction-I: the constituent SSH chains are topologically trivial with winding number $w=0$. Construction-II: the constituent SSH chains are topologically nontrivial with $w=1$. Although these constructions are unitarily equivalent in the static limit, circular driving distinguishes them because the hopping processes related by the transformation correspond to different physical bond vectors and therefore acquire different Peierls phases. Using the Floquet-Sambe formalism, we determine the quasienergy spectra and phase diagrams in terms of the lower-band Chern number $C_L$ and directional Zak phases $(Z_x,\, Z_y)$. We find distinct Floquet phase structures, including low-frequency phases with $C_L = -3$ and $C_L = -4$ in the two constructions. Since the Chern number does not resolve the topology of the two quasienergy gaps separately, we further calculate the dynamical winding numbers $W_0$ and $W_π$, and verify the corresponding chiral edge states. In particular, at identical driving parameters, both constructions can have the same Chern numbers $C_L=-2$, while their gap-resolved winding numbers are $(W_0,\, W_π)=(0,\,+2)$ and $(-2,\,0)$, respectively. We also calculate the time-averaged optical Hall conductivity and show that $ C_Le^2/h$ determines its dc value for ideal full-band occupation. At the same time, its finite-frequency response contains photon-assisted contributions. Our results demonstrate that the physical construction of the constituent chains, although irrelevant to the static bulk spectrum, can play a decisive role in the Floquet topological structure. We discuss possible experimental realizations of the driven model.

entries.title: Training-Free Instruction TTS Gender Bias Calibration Using Model-Adaptive Steering
entries.summary: Instruction text-to-speech (ITTS) systems systematically encode acoustic gender skews from descriptive style prompts, such as occupations or personas, even when demographic attributes are left unspecified. Calibrating the implicit gender distribution of the synthesized voices, across heterogeneous architectures and without model retraining or overriding explicit user prompts, is an open problem. In this work, we propose \textit{model-adaptive steering}, a training-free bias calibration method that steers post-encoder conditioning representations using a group deviation vector paired with a coarse-to-fine strength search on a development set. A deterministic lexical gate bypasses intervention whenever explicit gender keywords are detected, preserving intended prompt semantics. Evaluated on a 12,800-prompt held-out benchmark across four ITTS models (three architectures), the proposed method reduces aggregate calibration error from 11.5--28.1 to 0.8--5.9 percentage points (e.g., shifting Parler-TTS Mini from 78.1\% and PromptTTS++ from 27.3\% female to 50.8--52.4\%). Output rates stay within 0.9 pp across anchor set sizes at fixed operating points, while UTMOS decreases by at most 0.08 and WER degrades by at most 3.3 pp.

entries.title: LighTROcc: Lightweight 4D Occupancy Forecasting via Instance-Centric 3D Gaussians
entries.summary: Forecasting future 3D occupancy from surround-view cameras is essential for autonomous driving, yet existing approaches rely on dense voxel or bird's-eye-view representations whose cost grows rapidly with spatial resolution and prediction horizon. Because these representations do not explicitly maintain object identities, they also struggle to preserve instance consistency over time. We present LighTROcc, a lightweight instance-centric framework that represents movable objects with a compact set of learned queries and predicts present and future occupancy in a single forward pass. LighTROcc localizes each query through attention-guided forward lifting, combining image-space cross-attention, query-specific depth, and camera geometry to estimate its 3D center. Each instance is modeled as a mixture of anisotropic 3D Gaussians and propagated across future steps using predicted displacements, producing continuous, temporally consistent occupancy forecasts. Experiments on nuScenes and supplemented nuScenes-Occupancy show that LighTROcc outperforms the evaluated dense and instance-wise baselines in instance-level forecasting accuracy while maintaining strong voxel-level occupancy quality. Across different model configurations, LighTROcc achieves a favorable balance between forecasting accuracy and computational efficiency, demonstrating the potential of compact instance-centric modeling for camera-based 4D occupancy forecasting.

entries.title: Dungeon and Visibility World Generator
entries.summary: Robotic exploration, coverage, and multi-agent deployment algorithms require reproducible environments with controllable geometry and visibility. This paper presents the Dungeon and Visibility World Generator, an open-source framework for constructing two- and three-dimensional environments and evaluating geometric line-of-sight. The framework supports orthogonal, polygonal or polyhedral, and curvilinear geometries, with six construction families covering scattered rooms, clusters, winding passages, caverns, branches, and loops. Room dimensions, passage structures, obstacles, and spatial placement can be controlled through configurable parameters and probability distributions. Each generated environment provides continuous free-space geometry and a corresponding discrete occupancy representation. A Rust-based visibility engine supports line-of-sight queries in both representations, enabling the evaluation of observable regions from arbitrary agent positions. The framework records configurations, generated geometries, occupancy grids, and visibility results to support reproducible experiments. We demonstrate the generator across all six geometry classes, examine how geometry and spatial resolution affect visibility, and evaluate generation time and reproducibility. The resulting framework provides a configurable foundation for evaluating robotic exploration, coverage, and multi-agent deployment algorithms in diverse environments.

entries.title: Perception Beyond the Visible: Incompleteness-Aware Scene Understanding for Robot Autonomy
entries.summary: Reliable robot autonomy requires reasoning about the world from partial and noisy observations. However, many perception systems model only visible scene regions, rely on fixed semantic categories, and assume reliable sensor measurements. These assumptions break under occlusion, novel object encounters, and sensor degradation. In this paper, I present a research vision for incompleteness-aware scene understanding. I organize this vision around three fundamental challenges: incomplete evidence, incomplete knowledge, and incomplete sensor reliability. I discuss my research contributions toward addressing these challenges through amodal perception, semantic occupancy forecasting, open-world scene understanding, label-efficient learning, and uncertainty-guided multi-modal fusion. Building on these contributions, I outline future research directions toward belief-centric 4D scene representations. These representations aim to jointly model geometry, semantics, motion, and uncertainty. I also discuss active sensing and safe adaptation strategies that allow robots to reduce uncertainty through interaction. The goal is to develop calibrated and actionable scene representations that support reliable autonomy in dynamic, open-world environments.

entries.title: ReForesight: Occlusion-Robust Re-Identification and Future Occupancy Forecasting for Dynamic Semantic Mapping
entries.summary: Robots sharing walkways need to know where people will be, yet semantic occupancy maps show only where they are. We present ReForesight, an open-source ROS 2 toolkit that adds instance-level future occupancy and re-identification after occlusion to a particle-based semantic mapping pipeline. A 36.6k-parameter MLP predicts each tracked person or vehicle up to 3 s ahead, guarded by a Kalman fallback and a stationary gate, and the object's own points are moved to the forecast pose, forming a "ghost" point cloud in the map frame without an occupancy decoder. An optional tracker re-associates objects after occlusion using keypoint descriptors the pipeline already computes and a metric 3D gate. On four held-out CODa sequences, the MLP lowers the mean 3 s final displacement error from 0.728 m (Kalman) to 0.662 m and beats a similar-size GRU (0.692 m) on every sequence, at 0.04 ms per instance on one CPU core. Code, all models, and a ROS-free demo are released; field demonstrations use an outdoor cleaning robot.

entries.title: Towards Privacy-Preserving Thermal Human Perception from Dataset to Deployment
entries.summary: Indoor human perception is the foundation for smart homes and healthcare. However, RGB cameras raise privacy concerns in private indoor environments, while low-resolution thermal cameras provide limited spatial and semantic information. Large-scale indoor thermal datasets and real-world deployments remain limited. Here, we introduce Indoor RGB-T, a large-scale paired RGB--thermal dataset for indoor human perception. The dataset covers 20 indoor rooms and contains 90,576 80x62 thermal frames, 87,016 temporally matched RGB--thermal pairs, and 115,557 annotated human bounding boxes. We establish benchmarks for robust thermal occupant-state detection with 0.75 mAP and occupancy estimation with an accuracy of 0.847 in unseen rooms. We further evaluate RGB-to-thermal and thermal-to-RGB translation, achieving a temperature MAE of 0.654 C and an R2 of 0.923. Finally, we deploy the thermal perception model on a commercial sleep-monitoring system in the real world. Field testing with 100 participants and deployment of approximately 1,000 devices further demonstrate its practical feasibility. We identify practical challenges that motivate future research directions, including environmental thermal interference, sensing range and multi-person occlusion. The code, trained models and partial dataset are available at https://github.com/kailaisun/RGBT and https://huggingface.co/skl24/RGBT.

entries.title: CAST-ASD: Causal Attention over Speakers and Time for Online Active Speaker Detection
entries.summary: We present CAST-ASD (Causal Attention over Speakers and Time), a causal joint model for active speaker detection (ASD). Recent ASD models improve performance by jointly processing all faces in a scene, but operate offline, with the full clip available before any frame is labelled. Low-latency causal detectors instead process each face independently. CAST-ASD combines joint face reasoning with fully causal inference. It applies scene-level attention across faces within the current frame and causal temporal attention over each face's history, enabling information sharing across speakers with zero lookahead. Its parameter count does not grow with the number of faces. On MSDWild, where most negative face-frames contain a visible competing speaker, CAST-ASD reduces competing-speaker false alarms by 32% relative to the causal per-face detector it extends, with larger gains as scene occupancy increases. It outperforms all causal baselines on both validation splits while using only one-tenth the inter-speaker parameters of a three-block fixed-roster convolution. Code and models are available at https://github.com/prathamg007/CAST-ASD.

entries.title: Closing the Horizon Gap in Policy Optimization for Adversarial MDPs
entries.summary: We consider policy optimization for online episodic tabular Markov decision processes (MDPs) with adversarial losses and bandit feedback. Policy optimization updates the policy locally at each state and avoids optimization over the occupancy-measure polytope, but its existing regret bounds are larger by a factor of the horizon $H$ than those of occupancy-measure-based algorithms. We close this gap by using regularized $Q$-functions, which allow us to control the stability of the local updates jointly over all state-action pairs rather than separately at each state. The resulting algorithm attains high-probability regret bounds of $\widetilde O(\sqrt{HS(H+A)T})$ for known transitions and $\widetilde O(HS\sqrt{AT})$ for unknown transitions, where $S$ is the number of states, $A$ the number of actions, and $T$ the number of episodes. Both bounds improve the horizon dependence of existing policy optimization bounds, and the latter matches the best-known bound. We further extend the algorithm to adversarial linear-mixture MDPs and obtain the same improvement in the horizon dependence.

entries.title: Patient, Place, Prior (P$^3$): What Counts as Personalization in Medical World Models?
entries.summary: Longitudinal models forecast how a patient's imaging state evolves, but accuracy does not show whether the patient's observed trajectory drives the prediction. A population-average forecast may be useful but cannot establish a patient-specific world-model claim. We introduce Patient, Place, Prior (P$^3$), an audit asking whether a forecast benefits from the patient's longitudinal imaging history (Patient), benefits from patient-matched externally supplied spatial support (Place), and gains predictive value beyond a population-average prediction under matched support and context (Prior). We also propose Cancer JEPA, a one-step model that forecasts frozen representations of future breast dynamic contrast-enhanced MRI examinations during neoadjuvant therapy. It adds a lesion-constrained neural correction, trained with an occlusion-based latent objective, to a patient-conditioned low-complexity reduced-rank regression baseline. This factorization permits a post-hoc P$^3$ audit of the frozen model. In a validation cohort previously used in development, forecast error is lower when the neural correction receives the patient's history rather than another patient's and patient-matched lesion occupancy maps rather than substituted maps. However, the descriptive 95% interval comparing the correction computed from patient history with the population-average neural correction includes zero. P$^3$ thus separates input use from evidence of patient-specific predictive value beyond a population-level pattern.

entries.title: Efficient Learning of Structured Fermionic States under General Quadratic Evolution
entries.summary: We prove copy-optimal learning of the full Gaussian orbit of paired magic states on $n$ fermionic modes. The unknown evolution may be any parity-preserving quadratic circuit, including pair creation and annihilation, and each copy is measured once, in a fixed basis, on a single quartic Majorana observable. A nonadaptive learner returns a Gaussian preparation within trace distance $ε$ from $Θ(n^6/ε^2)$ copies at fixed confidence, and no learner in this measurement model, adaptive or not, can do better. Measured quartic correlations certify the trace distance of the result. Our second result extends learning to a broader family: pure states whose unknown input blocks are superpositions of disjoint occupation patterns with bounded particle number, under the same evolution. Using single-copy Gaussian rotations and occupation readout, a batch-adaptive learner returns an input and a Gaussian circuit with infidelity $f$ from $\widetilde O(n^7/f)$ copies and polynomial classical processing. Connected quartic correlations reveal the hidden mode groups, and fresh local measurements restore the branches and their coherences. No particle-number conservation, minimum branch weight or spectral gap is assumed.

entries.title: An RFSoC-Based 100 GbE Spectrometer/Correlator for the Baryon Mapping Experiment: Digital Backend Design and On-Sky Validation
entries.summary: We describe the implementation and on-sky commissioning of a two-input spectrometer/correlator built on a Xilinx ZCU208 Radio Frequency System-on-Chip (RFSoC) and deployed on the Baryon Mapping eXperiment (BMX) interferometric array at Brookhaven National Laboratory. The system combines direct RF sampling, FPGA-based correlation, and 100 Gigabit Ethernet (GbE) visibility transport. Two inputs are digitized directly at 1050 MHz without analog downconversion and channelized into 2048 frequency channels. The correlator forms two autocorrelations and the real and imaginary parts of the cross-correlation, accumulates them in on-chip memory, and transmits the spectra as UDP packets at a fixed firmware-controlled rate. Two independent campaigns using 500 ms and 100 ms accumulation times produced 958,918 consecutive accumulations with no lost, duplicated, or malformed packets. A Cauchy-Schwarz bound is satisfied across all 1.96e9 channel-samples, confirming correct field identification and scaling. On-sky validation includes compact-source transits in six GNSS bands with the expected fringes, coherent detection of the Cygnus A zenith transit at the predicted time, and a Galactic HI plane crossing detected independently in autocorrelation on both dishes. The correlator is parameterizable in input count, with arithmetic scaling quadratically. For extension to BMX's full eight-input dual-polarization system, an occupancy model validated against the deployed firmware indicates that visibility buffering fits when moved to UltraRAM, while multi-tile synchronization, logic utilization, and timing closure remain to be demonstrated in an eight-input implementation.

entries.title: Mean squared error reduction of (plug-in) look-ahead estimators for Markov chains
entries.summary: We consider the estimation of the invariant distribution $π$ of a Markov kernel on a discrete state space (or of the mean value $π(f)$ of a functional $f$ under $π$) when solving the invariance equation is not feasible. Look-ahead estimators exploit the knowledge of the kernel by propagating the empirical occupation measure through $k$ steps of the chain. When the kernel is known, as in Markov chain Monte Carlo, we compare their mean squared error with that of the empirical estimator, for independent or Markovian data, stationary or not. Our main result establishes that, for Markovian data, the one-step estimator always improves on the empirical one asymptotically, and that the improvement grows with $k$ for reversible kernels. A non-reversible counterexample shows that reversibility cannot simply be dropped. In the statistical setting where the kernel belongs to a parametric family with unknown parameter, we introduce plug-in look-ahead estimators, which perform the look-ahead step with an estimated kernel. When the parameter is estimated at the parametric rate, we give a necessary and sufficient condition under which the plug-in look-ahead estimator outperforms the empirical one. The theoretical results are illustrated by extensive simulation studies, which also shed further light on the behaviour of the estimators at hand. Both settings are finally applied to real data arising from geographical mobility problems in the Lyon metropolitan area, France.

entries.title: Return-to-Home Feasible Micro-Aerial Vehicle Exploration for 3D Gaussian Splatting Reconstruction
entries.summary: Micro aerial vehicles (MAVs) enable rapid indoor 3D reconstruction for inspection and time-critical situational awareness, but must operate under strict flight-time budgets and safety constraints that require explicit return-to-home (RTH) feasibility with a conservative margin. We present a topology-first active reconstruction framework that decouples high-fidelity rendering from navigation. A dense 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) map is optimized as the reconstruction target, while a lightweight Truncated Signed Distance Field (TSDF)/occupancy scaffold supports conservative collision checking and online construction of a sparse 3D Voronoi skeleton roadmap. Since directly extracting roadmaps from TSDF geometry can be unstable under noisy and incomplete online fusion, we validate nodes and edges using carved free-space consistency and dense visibility checks, which suppress behind-wall phantom structure and stabilize planning. Viewpoints are selected on the roadmap using a flight-time-budget-aware objective and a lightweight receding-horizon lookahead to improve non-myopic exploration behavior. We evaluate on photorealistic indoor simulation benchmarks (ReplicaCAD, Gibson, and HM3D), reporting reconstruction coverage/error, RTH success, and computational cost. Results demonstrate improved or competitive performance relative to recent GS-based baselines under identical flight-time budgets.

entries.title: CrowdOcc: Monocular Semantic Scene Completion for Quadruped Robots in Crowded Indoor Environments
entries.summary: Monocular semantic scene completion (SSC) for quadruped robots remains underexplored in real crowded indoor environments, where human-scene occlusion disrupts static geometry and human occupancy predictions are often incomplete or spatially misplaced. We present CrowdOcc, an RGB-D dataset and monocular SSC framework for this setting. CrowdOcc contains 25.1K frames from 11 indoor scenes, with semantic occupancy annotations constructed through static dynamic decoupling. Our framework combines: (i) Normal Guided Scene Geometry Fusion (NGSGF) to complement depth-aware lifting with surface-normal cues for occlusion robust geometry; and (ii) Human-Centric Sparse Interaction (HCSI) to selectively model human-human and local human scene relations in 3D. Our method achieves state-of-the-art SSC performance on CrowdOcc's scene-disjoint test set, reaching 15.80 IoU, 11.40 mIoU, and 46.23 Human IoU, demonstrating generalization to unseen indoor scenes.

entries.title: Exact random centering and hybrid fluctuation limits for interacting reinforced processes under critical Markov switching
entries.summary: We study two interacting reinforced occupation processes driven by a common two-state Markov environment whose switching probabilities decrease at the same rate as the stochastic-approximation gain. At this critical scale, the environmental motion persists in the first-order limit, which is a telegraph-driven piecewise deterministic Markov process. Consequently, centering at a deterministic equilibrium does not separate the order-one environmental response from the intrinsic square-root fluctuations. To overcome this obstruction, we introduce an exact discrete random centering that removes the accumulated environmental forcing before rescaling. An exact decomposition into collective and synchronization coordinates then separates the two contraction mechanisms of the system. Under the contraction condition corresponding to the square-root regime, we prove joint functional convergence of the randomly centered coordinates and the first-order background to a stationary hybrid PDMP--diffusion system. Its stationary entrance law is characterized through stochastic convolutions over the remote logarithmic past. Conditionally on the complete environmental path, the two fluctuation modes are independent centered Gaussian processes with a common state-dependent volatility and different contraction rates. We also determine the invariant distribution of the first-order component, derive explicit stationary second moments, and obtain a closed-form correlation formula that recovers interaction information not visible in the synchronized first-order limit.

entries.title: Fully Online Decentralized Learning in Stochastic Games with Unknown Independent Chains
entries.summary: We consider stochastic games with independent controlled chains and unknown transition kernels, where players observe only their local states and realized payoffs. We develop a fully online, decentralized, and uncoordinated mirror-descent algorithm that operates in the dual space of occupancy measures for approximating stationary Nash equilibrium (NE) policies. The algorithm uses a single transition/reward sample at every primitive time step, relies only on local information, and requires neither coverage of the joint state space nor synchronized episodes. Under uniform-ergodicity and finite-coverage assumptions, we show that, with high probability, the time-averaged fixed-comparator regret decays at the canonical $O(T^{-1/2})$ rate, up to logarithmic factors and polynomial dependence on the game parameters. In particular, the complexity depends on the cover times of the individual local state spaces rather than the product state space, avoiding exponential dependence on the number of players and the sizes of the joint state and action spaces. The resulting finite-time regret bound further yields an approximate coarse-correlated-equilibrium guarantee, which is natural for arbitrary reward functions since computing a stationary $ε$-NE is PPAD-hard in this setting. Under an additional global variational-stability condition, we show that the same fully online algorithm converges asymptotically in the last iterate to a stationary $ε$-NE. Our results provide a fully online and scalable learning framework for stochastic games with unknown independent chains. The algorithm can also be viewed as a primal-dual framework for Markov games that exploits the independence and local structure of the players' controlled transition chains.

entries.title: Active Mapping of Underwater Litter Using Camera-Sonar Fusion
entries.summary: Marine litter is a growing threat to the underwater ecosystem, driving demand for autonomous survey methods that can locate debris efficiently over large areas. Existing survey methods typically follow predefined paths or operate with a single sensing modality, typically a camera (with image quality suffering in poor-visibility conditions) or sonar (usually noisy and low-resolution). We present an active mapping framework in which a forward-looking sonar and a camera both feed into a shared Bayesian occupancy map, and an optimization problem is solved at each step to decide on the next best view. Candidate viewpoints are scored by a two-term utility that balances exploration of uncertain regions via voxel entropy against exploitation of likely objects. Each sensor is characterized by range- and bearing-dependent detection and false-alarm probability tables determined from data. We evaluate the approach in a realistic underwater simulator, demonstrating that active mapping finds objects faster than a lawnmower coverage pattern, and that the dual-sensor approach works better than using either of the individual sensors.

entries.title: Beyond the Remembered World: Predictive 4D Belief for Persistent Navigation in Evolving Worlds
entries.summary: Persistent spatial memory enables embodied agents to navigate familiar environments across repeated visits. However, targets may move while unobserved, including during navigation, making remembered locations unreliable by the time an agent arrives. Despite advances in memory retrieval and state prediction, accounting for continued hidden world evolution and revising beliefs under limited visibility remain challenging. We study Evolving-World Navigation, where agents infer target locations from intermittent observations, predict their states at inspection time, and revise beliefs using visual evidence. We propose EvolvingNav, which constructs a time-indexed belief from timestamped 3D object histories through a structured persistence-relocation model. The belief distinguishes persistence at the last observed location from relocation to alternative locations and retains probability mass outside the known candidate set. An event-driven filter propagates the current belief as time elapses, forecasts target occupancy at candidate inspection times, and incorporates new RGB-D evidence. Negative observations downweight location hypotheses according to calibrated, visibility-conditioned detection probabilities, while evidence tracking prevents repeated use of the same observations. A frozen, zero-shot vision-language controller uses the updated belief to choose actions and replan. We further introduce EvoWorld-Bench, a benchmark grounded in human activity traces, comprising 54 scenes and 803,680 tasks with controlled changes before and during navigation. In simulation and real-robot experiments, EvolvingNav improves navigation success and search efficiency over the evaluated baselines. Paired experiments show the clearest gains under learnable temporal patterns, while ablations demonstrate the value of preserving uncertainty and incorporating visibility-aware evidence.

entries.title: Planning Oriented 3D Scene Completion via Coupled TUDF Occupancy Representation Learning from Partial Observations
entries.summary: Partial observability remains a fundamental challenge in robotic navigation, where limited sensor coverage and occlusions leave large portions of the environment unobserved. Existing scene completion methods primarily focus on improving incomplete mapping or reconstructing partially observed 3D structures, but rarely investigate how scene completion can be designed to benefit downstream tasks such as path planning. In this work, we propose a path-planning-oriented 3D scene completion framework that moves beyond pure occupancy modeling toward a coupled geometric formulation. Specifically, given partial LiDAR observations as input, the proposed framework jointly predicts completed Truncated Unsigned Distance Field (TUDF)-based continuous geometric representations and voxel-wise occupancy maps. This coupled representation allows the network to better reason about obstacle boundaries and free-space geometry. To fully exploit the synergy between the two representations, we introduce a bidirectionally coupled learning scheme, where TUDF features provide dense geometric guidance to improve occupancy reconstruction, while occupancy features in turn offer complementary structural constraints that refine distance-field estimation. Consequently, the proposed network directly predicts complete occupancy and TUDF representations, allowing seamless integration of TUDF into trajectory planning without post-processing. Extensive experiments on unseen environments demonstrate that the proposed method consistently improves both geometric reconstruction quality and downstream planning performance.

entries.title: Asymmetric imaging: Reciprocity bounds and manifestations
entries.summary: Recent demonstrations of unidirectional imaging using diffractive multilayers have brought a concept akin to optical isolation to imaging, yet the fundamental limits of such asymmetry have remained unknown. Here we develop a general theory of asymmetric imaging in linear, passive, reciprocal optical systems and derive a fundamental bound on the achievable unidirectionality. Reciprocity requires the forward and reverse transmission operators to have identical singular values, a wave-optical analogue of étendue equality, with a simple consequence: perfect asymmetry is attainable only for sets of $M \leq N/2$ orthogonal object patterns, where $N$ is the number of available object/image modes; for $M > N/2$, the average power asymmetry is bounded by $(N-M)/M$. Guided by this result, we present two complementary realizations: refractive imaging systems formed by bulk lenses and stops that attain the half-occupation limit, and a 1 cm-diameter all-silicon metasurface doublet that exhibits asymmetric focusing at 4 $μ$m while fully complying with Lorentz reciprocity. We fabricate the doublet by direct laser writing and experimentally demonstrate its focusing asymmetry. By establishing mechanism-independent limits, our results provide a benchmark and design principle for asymmetric imaging across platforms, with implications for defense, surveillance and secure communications.

entries.title: Improved Modeling for Moving Sources of Radio Frequency Interference and Impact on Flagging Strategies
entries.summary: Radio frequency interference (RFI) is a major challenge for low-frequency radio experiments targeting the redshifted 21-cm signal from the Epoch of Reionization. Many important RFI sources, including aircraft and satellites, move across the sky during an observation. The averaging of visibilities for such moving sources over a finite correlator integration produces a distinct sinc-like pattern in the interferometric uv-plane, causing the RFI to appear bright on some baselines and strongly suppressed on others. Here, we develop an analytical model for this effect and validate its qualitative behavior against real MWA observations and numerical simulations. Controlled RFI injections into clean MWA data are then used to compare several flagging treatments in the context of EoR power spectrum recovery. These treatments explore the trade-off between per-baseline flagging, which can miss weak but potentially non-negligible contamination on baselines where the integration effect leads to strong suppression, and baseline-aggregated flagging, which removes more faint residual contamination but reduces the total number of usable uv-modes. We find that the preferred strategy depends on RFI brightness and occupancy, but that flagging all frequencies at contaminated time-steps most consistently minimizes excess power for bright or frequent events. However, none of the tested flagging treatments fully recovers the uncontaminated reference spectrum, motivating future work on direct modeling and subtraction of moving RFI sources.

entries.title: Beyond Conservatism: Recoverability-Conditioned Exploration for Model-Based Imitation Learning
entries.summary: Model-based imitation learning (MBIL) improves real-environment interaction efficiency by optimizing policies on imagined rollouts from a learned world model. However, the gap between model-induced and real-environment occupancies makes policy learning sensitive to model error. Conservative MBIL mitigates model exploitation during policy optimization, but when real-environment interactions are collected by the same conservative policy, uncertain regions around the expert distribution remain insufficiently sampled. Generic uncertainty-driven exploration, on the other hand, may allocate interaction to novel but task-irrelevant dynamics. We propose REcoverability-CONditioned Exploration for Model-Based Imitation Learning (RECON). RECON separates conservative policy learning from active data collection by maintaining a main policy for task execution and an explorer for real-environment interaction. The explorer is optimized based on epistemic uncertainty conditioned on recoverability estimated from multi-step main-policy imagination, focusing data collection on unknown states from which the main policy can still return toward expert behavior. Experiments on locomotion, navigation and manipulation show consistent gains in interaction efficiency, imitation performance, and robustness, indicating that RECON directs real-environment interaction toward recovery regions around the expert distribution that are underexplored by prior methods, and thereby learns a world model better suited for imitation.
